messages:
maria: heads up — seeing intermittent link flaps and RX errors on a1dn hosts in us-west-2 after the bnxt fw push earlier this morning. ~30 hosts affected across two AZs.

deploy-bot: rollout bnxt-fw v2.1.4 to a1dn pool started at 1768459200, 5% increments.

aj: looking at a1dn-672 now — dmesg spam: 'bnxt_en: TX prep failed, queue 3' and 'bnxt_en: VF reset requested by PF' then interface resets. rx_errors++ counters jumping during the window.

raj: grabbed tcpdump on a1dn-672 — lots of out-of-order / retransmit bursts. MTU across some subnets is 9000 but not consistently applied; also saw large coalesced packets. Could be LRO/GRO interaction.

maria: we changed MTU to 9000 for p4d flows last night but only applied to the compute-subnet, not the infra-subnet. possible mismatch between hosts and top-of-rack.

kevin: on older bnxt firmwares jumbo+LRO can trigger RX checksum / fragment handling bugs. quick mitigation: disable LRO/GRO on affected NICs.

aj: confirmed — toggling LRO cleared the rx_errors on host I tested. command I ran: 
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 lro off gro off
sudo systemctl restart network-monitor
```
errors fell to baseline in ~90s.

raj: we should decide rollback vs vendor patch. rollback to v2.1.3 on a canary set and monitor.

maria: propose rollback 10 hosts in us-west-2 AZ-b now, collect pcaps and dmesg, open vendor ticket with traces. If rollback fixes, do staged rollback for the rest.

ops-bot: INC created: INC-2026-847 — bnxt-fw v2.1.4 causing RX/TX errors in us-west-2. severity: minor. assignees: @maria, @aj.

deploy-bot: executing rollback bnxt-fw -> v2.1.3 on a1dn-azb group (10 hosts) at 1768460000.

aj: rollback completed on 10 hosts. counters dropped back to baseline within 2m on all of them. no link flaps observed post-rollback.

kevin: do not re-enable LRO until vendor confirms fix. also capture perf metrics for both configurations (LRO on/off) so we can quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.

maria: filing vendor ticket with traces, sample hosts, ethtool outputs, and pcap. if vendor response >24h, we'll schedule full rollback for remaining 40 hosts.

raj: long-term: add pre-deploy smoke tests for NIC firmware pushes — small-batch iperf east-west, simple pcap + BPF counter check for rx_errors, and MTU verification across subnets.

maria: agreed. I'll put the checklist in the release playbook and share the affected-host list + pcaps in the incident doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
